property_summary: Calling deposit with value v does not revert (always succeeds) for any caller and value.
If deposit reverts then it must be because the test contract lacked sufficient Ether to send that value (i.e., deposit only reverts when the provided value exceeds the tester's balance).

For any caller and ether value, if deposit(...) reverts then the sent value was greater than zero and the call reverted only because the addition would overflow uint256 (which cannot happen in P due to the explicit assert), so in P deposit never reverts solely from an overflow — equivalently, if deposit reverts then value == 0 is false but in M it may succeed where P would revert.

Calling deposit with any value never reverts in the original contract C (because its assert prevents overflow), but the mutant can allow an overflow-free call that would have reverted in C; therefore deposit should never revert for any caller/value that fits within this contract's balance constraints.

For any caller and any deposit value, after a successful deposit() call the contract's recorded balance for that caller is equal to the sum of its previous recorded balance and the deposited value; removing the overflow check can allow an overflow so this invariant can be violated for some inputs.

For any caller and deposit value, after deposit() returns successfully the contract's recorded balance for that caller is at least as large as it was before plus the deposited amount (i.e., balances[msg.sender]_after >= balances[msg.sender]_before + value); removing the overflow check can allow wrapping so this monotonic increase property is violated for some inputs.

For any caller and deposit amount, calling deposit() never decreases the caller's recorded balance compared to before the call (i.e., balances_after >= balances_before); removing the overflow check allows an overflow that can make balances_after < balances_before for some fuzzed amount and caller.

For any depositor and deposit amount, if deposit() returns successfully then the stored balances(depositor) is strictly greater than its previous value (the reference prevents addition wrapping); the mutant that removed the overflow check allows wrapping so for some depositor and amount the post-deposit stored balance is not greater than the pre-deposit value.

For any depositor and deposit value, if deposit() returns successfully then the contract's recorded balance for that depositor equals the previous recorded balance plus the deposited amount (no silent wraparound); removing the overflow-assert allows an input that causes wrapping so this equality can fail.
After a deposit of value v from caller, the contract's recorded balance for that caller is at least as large as the ETH value sent (i.e. balances[msg.sender] increased by >= v).

If the caller sends a positive amount of ETH to deposit (and the test has that ETH), the deposit call must not revert (i.e., reverted == false).

For any caller and any deposit amount, after calling deposit() the stored balances[caller] is at least the previous stored value (i.e., deposit never decreases the recorded balance); the mutant that subtracts the amount can make the stored balance decrease for some caller/amount, violating this rule.

After calling deposit(x) the contract's balance increases by exactly x (i.e., address(c).balance == old_balance + x).
For any deposit value > 0, deposit never causes an assertion failure (i.e., deposit completes without reverting) when called by any address.

After a deposit of any amount by any address, the call either succeeds and increases the contract balance by that amount, or it reverts (no silent assertion failure); specifically, the deposit call must not trigger an internal assert when the sender supplied msg.value equal to the amount.

property_summary: A successful deposit call (non-reverting) must increase the contract's ether balance by exactly the sent value.

If a deposit call with positive msg.value succeeds, then a subsequent deposit of any positive value (by the same caller) that also succeeds leaves the second call non-reverting (i.e., both succeed) — deposit cannot depend on zeroing previous balance.

For any caller and any positive msg.value, calling deposit() increases that caller's recorded balance by exactly msg.value on the reference contract; the mutant resets the prior balance to zero before adding msg.value and thus can make the final recorded balance smaller than prior+msg.value (violating the increase rule) for callers with a pre-existing nonzero balance.

For any caller and any deposit amount > 0, calling deposit increases that caller's recorded balance by exactly the deposited amount (final_balance == prior_balance + msg.value) in the reference; the mutant resets prior_balance to zero before adding msg.value, breaking this rule when prior_balance > 0.

For any caller and any deposit amount > 0, after deposit() the contract's recorded balance for that caller equals the prior recorded balance plus the deposited amount; the mutant resets prior balance to zero before adding msg.value and thus can make final_balance != prior + msg.value when prior > 0.

For any actor and any nonzero deposit amount, calling deposit increases that actor's recorded balance by at least the deposited amount (final_balance >= prior_balance + msg.value); the mutant resets prior balance to zero before adding msg.value, so when prior_balance > 0 the mutant can make final_balance < prior_balance + msg.value.

For any actor and any deposit amount, if the actor makes two consecutive deposits, the second deposit increases the actor's recorded balance by exactly the second deposit amount (i.e., final_balance_after_second == balance_after_first + second_amount); the mutant resets the prior balance to zero before adding msg.value and thus can make the second deposit not add on top of the first when the first left a nonzero balance.
